parsed.rationale: Both `AsyncNotificationMessage` (in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/AsyncMessage.swift`) and `MainActorNotificationMessage` (in `Shared/Core/Sources/Core/Observation/MainActorMessage.swift`) are interfaces in the same `Core` package sharing 3 of 3 members: `name: Notification.Name`, `makeNotification(_ message: Self, object: Subject?) -> Notification`, and a `makeMessage` factory. The sole structural difference is that `MainActorNotificationMessage.makeMessage` annotates its parameter as `sending Notification` (for actor-isolation transfer), while `AsyncNotificationMessage` omits that qualifier. Introducing a base PAT `NotificationMessage` with the shared `name` and `makeNotification` requirements — and letting each child protocol refine `makeMessage` with its own concurrency annotation — eliminates the duplicated surface while preserving the distinct isolation semantics. Both protocols live in the same package and neither carries any restraint markers, making this a clean, low-risk consolidation.
